blocks.text: Filter Methods introduced the genuine general idea, scoring each feature statistical relevance independently of any model. Correlation is the first, and most familiar, specific technique in that family, directly reusing the Pearson correlation coefficient first covered back in Correlation Analysis, now applied specifically to the practical task of deciding which features to actually keep.

This topic covers the two genuinely distinct ways correlation gets used for feature selection, ranking features by their relevance to the target and catching redundant features that duplicate each other, a direct recap of what the correlation coefficient itself measures, a real, important limitation, correlation only captures linear relationships, and the correlation heatmap as the practical, visual tool for applying both uses at once.
1. Two Genuinely Distinct Uses of Correlation Here

blocks.alt: Two Genuinely Distinct Uses of Correlation Here
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443279792-726774305.png

Feature to target correlation genuinely measures relevance, how strongly a numeric feature relates to the numeric target, directly informing which features are genuinely worth keeping for their own predictive value. Feature to feature correlation genuinely measures redundancy instead, how strongly two input features relate to each other, regardless of either one relationship to the target.

These are genuinely two separate, complementary questions, and both matter for a complete feature selection pass, one identifies genuinely valuable features, the other identifies genuinely duplicated ones among those that already look valuable.
2. Relevance: Ranking Features by Target Correlation

blocks.alt: Relevance: Ranking Features by Target Correlation
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443279792-283777635.png

For every genuine numeric feature, computing its correlation with the numeric target and ranking features by the genuine absolute value of that correlation, ignoring sign, directly identifies which features carry the strongest real, linear relationship to what is actually being predicted. The genuine top ranked features are kept, and the weakest are dropped.

This is genuinely the most direct, simplest application of correlation to feature selection, and it connects immediately back to the feature to target relationships first explored visually in Bivariate Analysis, now turned into a precise, rankable score.
3. Redundancy: Dropping Highly Correlated Feature Pairs

blocks.alt: Redundancy: Dropping Highly Correlated Feature Pairs
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443279793-177282795.png

When two input features are genuinely highly correlated with each other, total rooms and bedrooms plus bathrooms, the exact example first covered back in Feature Relationships, they carry largely genuine duplicate information. Keeping both offers genuinely little additional value over keeping just one, and can even cause real problems for certain models, exactly the multicollinearity concern covered in that earlier topic.

The genuinely standard fix is dropping one feature from each highly correlated pair, typically the one with genuinely weaker correlation to the target, keeping the more informative of the two while removing the real redundancy.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: When dropping one of a highly correlated pair, genuinely keep the one with the stronger relationship to the target. This combines both uses of correlation covered in this topic into a single, sensible decision.

blocks.text: 4. A Worked Example
Computing both feature to target and feature to feature correlation with pandas shows both genuine uses side by side, on a small house sales dataset.

code.content:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "square_feet": [900, 1200, 1500, 1800, 2100],
    "total_rooms": [3, 4, 5, 6, 7],
    "bedrooms_plus_baths": [3, 4, 5, 6, 7],
    "price": [250000, 310000, 360000, 410000, 460000],
})

print(df.corr()["price"])
print("Feature to feature:", df["total_rooms"].corr(df["bedrooms_plus_baths"]))

blocks.text: All three features genuinely correlate strongly with price here, but total_rooms and bedrooms_plus_baths also genuinely correlate almost perfectly with each other, exactly the redundancy signal that argues for dropping one of that pair before moving forward.

blocks.text: 5. A Direct Recap: What Correlation Actually Measures

blocks.alt: A Direct Recap: What Correlation Actually Measures
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443279793-706773736.png

The Pearson correlation coefficient, covered in full back in Correlation Analysis, genuinely ranges from negative 1 to positive 1, with its sign showing genuine direction, positive meaning both variables rise together, negative meaning one rises as the other falls, and its magnitude showing genuine strength, values closer to either extreme indicating a genuinely stronger relationship.

This recap matters directly here, feature selection using correlation is genuinely just this same familiar statistic, applied specifically and repeatedly across every feature in a dataset, rather than examined one pair at a time as in that earlier, more exploratory topic.
6. A Real, Important Limitation: Linear Relationships Only

blocks.alt: A Real, Important Limitation: Linear Relationships Only
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443279793-74197715.png

Correlation genuinely only captures linear relationships well, a genuinely real, strong relationship that happens to be curved or cyclical can produce a correlation coefficient genuinely close to zero, making that feature look irrelevant by this measure even though it may genuinely carry real, useful signal, exactly the kind of nonlinear pattern first discussed back in Bivariate Analysis scatter plot patterns.

This is a genuinely real, practical risk worth taking seriously, correlation based filtering can genuinely discard a feature that would have been valuable to a model capable of capturing nonlinear patterns, tree based models in particular, covered later in this course.

blocks.text: 7. The Correlation Heatmap as a Practical Tool

blocks.alt: The Correlation Heatmap as a Practical Tool
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443279793-281527153.png

For a dataset with many numeric features, a correlation heatmap, first introduced back in Multivariate Analysis, condenses every pairwise correlation into a single, genuinely scannable grid, letting both relevance, the row or column for the target, and redundancy, any two features both showing high correlation with each other, be checked visually at once.

This is genuinely the most practical, common way correlation based feature selection actually gets applied in a real project, one heatmap covering both of this topic genuine uses simultaneously, rather than computing each pairwise correlation individually by hand.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: When scanning a correlation heatmap, genuinely check the target row or column first for relevance, then scan the rest of the grid for any pair of input features that are also highly correlated with each other.

blocks.text: 8. Correlation Versus What Comes Next
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443279793-29138847.png

Correlation genuinely handles the numeric feature, numeric target case well, but it structurally cannot apply to categorical data at all, correlation requires genuine numbers to compute a meaningful coefficient from. Most real datasets genuinely mix numeric and categorical features together, exactly the case the next topic addresses.

Chi-Square, covered next, fills exactly that gap, a genuine statistical test built specifically for measuring the relationship between two categorical variables, extending this module filter method toolkit beyond the purely numeric case covered here.

items: Correlation for feature selection genuinely serves two purposes: ranking relevance and catching redundancy.
Feature to target correlation genuinely ranks features by their absolute relationship strength with the target.
Feature to feature correlation genuinely identifies redundant pairs, connecting directly to Feature Relationships.
The Pearson coefficient genuinely ranges from negative 1 to positive 1, sign for direction, magnitude for strength.
Correlation genuinely only captures linear relationships well, risking discarding real, nonlinear signal.
A correlation heatmap is the genuine, practical tool applying both relevance and redundancy checks at once.
